attractions.name: Ellora Caves
attractions.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site of 34 Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut caves carved into a basalt cliff.
about: Ellora Caves are among the most important historical attractions in Maharashtra and are inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The site holds 34 major rock-cut caves, temples and monasteries carved out of a basalt cliff, representing the Buddhist, Hindu and Jain traditions side by side.

The complex developed between roughly the 6th and 10th centuries CE, and its best known monument is Cave 16, the Kailasa Temple, carved out of a single mass of rock. Together the caves are an extraordinary record of ancient Indian architecture, sculpture, religion and engineering.
highlights: 34 rock-cut caves along a basalt cliff
Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments in one complex
Sculptural panels and carved pillared halls
whyVisit: A full day of heritage exploration close to the hotel

attractions.name: Kailasa Temple – Ellora
attractions.description: Cave 16 at Ellora: a monumental temple to Lord Shiva carved out of a single rock.
about: Kailasa Temple sits in Cave 16 of the Ellora complex and is considered one of the most remarkable achievements of ancient Indian rock-cut architecture. The entire temple was carved downwards out of a single rock mass rather than built up from stone blocks.

The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is traditionally associated with the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I in the 8th century. Its enormous courtyard, Nandi Mandapa, towering shikhara and carved panels from the Ramayana and Mahabharata give visitors an extraordinary sense of the craftsmanship of the period.
whyVisit: One of the greatest works of Indian rock-cut architecture
The most iconic monument of Ellora

attractions.name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
attractions.description: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, in Verul beside the Ellora heritage complex.
about: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga Temple in Verul is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations of the region.

The present temple is built in red volcanic stone with a beautifully carved five-tiered shikhara and a twenty-four pillared assembly hall. Its pillars and walls carry detailed sculptures and mythological artwork, and the temple in its current form is largely associated with the 18th-century restoration works of Ahilyabai Holkar.
whyVisit: Deeply spiritual atmosphere, ideal early in the morning

attractions.name: Lakshvinayak Ganpati Temple – Verul
attractions.description: A revered Ganesha shrine at Verul, counted among the traditional Ganpati Kshetras.
about: Shri Lakshvinayak Ganpati Temple at Verul is an important Ganesha shrine and is traditionally counted among the twenty-one significant Ganpati Kshetras.

Its location beside Grishneshwar Temple and the Ellora Caves makes it an easy and peaceful spiritual stop for devotees exploring the Verul area, and its local religious traditions place it among the important shrines of the region.
highlights: Counted among the traditional Ganpati Kshetras
whyVisit: A calm spiritual stop near Ellora and Grishneshwar
Easy to combine with the Ellora sightseeing circuit

attractions.name: Bhadra Maruti Temple – Khultabad
attractions.description: A famous Hanuman temple at Khultabad, known for its rare reclining idol of Lord Hanuman.
about: Bhadra Maruti Temple at Khultabad is a well-known shrine dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Its most distinctive feature is the idol of Hanuman in a reclining or sleeping posture, known as Bhava Samadhi, a form rarely seen elsewhere.

Local tradition connects the temple with the devotion of King Bhadrasen and the legends associated with Lord Hanuman. The temple architecture also carries a mix of North Indian and South Indian influences, and it remains an important stop on the Khultabad–Ellora pilgrimage circuit.
highlights: Rare reclining idol of Lord Hanuman
Bhava Samadhi form of the deity
Blend of North and South Indian temple styles
whyVisit: Distinctive temple architecture and local traditions

attractions.name: Maheshmal Balaji Temple
attractions.description: A Lord Venkatesha temple set in the green hills of Maheshmal, often called the Tirupati of Marathwada.
about: Maheshmal Balaji Temple is dedicated to Lord Venkatesha and stands in the scenic hill area of Maheshmal, which is often described as the Tirupati of Marathwada.

The main deity is described as a replica of the deity at Tirupati Balaji, and worship here follows Tirupati-style traditions. Maheshmal itself is known for its greenery, cooler climate and views over the surrounding landscape, so a visit combines pilgrimage with a hill-country outing.
highlights: Green hill setting with cool weather
Scenic views over the surrounding hills

attractions.name: Daulatabad Fort / Devgiri Fort
attractions.description: A medieval hill fortress famed for its defences, Chand Minar and panoramic Deccan views.
about: Daulatabad Fort, historically known as Devagiri, is one of the most impressive medieval fortresses in Maharashtra, built around a steep conical hill. Its original development is associated with the Yadava ruler Bhillama V in the 12th century, and in 1327 Muhammad bin Tughluq famously ordered the shifting of his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.

The fort is remarkable for its defensive design: narrow winding approaches, massive walls, moats, gates, rock-cut passages and steep slopes that together made it extremely difficult to capture. Chand Minar, Chini Mahal, the Baradari and the dark Andheri Passage are among its best known features.
highlights: Medieval hill fortress on a conical hill
The Andheri Passage and rock-cut defences
whyVisit: A memorable climb with sweeping views
Rich layers of Yadava and Tughluq history

attractions.name: Panchakki – Water Mill
attractions.description: A medieval water mill in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, powered by water carried from a distant source.
about: Panchakki is a historic water mill in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, part of the complex associated with the Sufi saint Baba Shah Musafir. It is an excellent example of medieval hydraulic engineering.

An underground conduit brought water from a distant source into a reservoir; water falling into the cistern generated the power that drove the mill. The complex also includes a large reservoir, fountains, garden areas and tombs linked to the Sufi tradition of the site.
whyVisit: Calm, shaded surroundings in the city

attractions.name: Shri Vishwakarma Teerth Dham – Giant Shivling, Verul
attractions.description: A distinctive modern Shiva temple at Verul built in the form of a giant Shivling.
about: Shri Vishwakarma Teerth Dham at Verul is a distinctive modern Shiva pilgrimage site near the Ellora and Grishneshwar area, developed as a large temple complex in the shape of a Shivling.

The complex also incorporates representations of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and its design combines traditional Shiva symbolism with modern temple architecture, which makes it a popular stop for visitors touring Verul.
highlights: Temple built in the form of a giant Shivling
whyVisit: Close to the major heritage sites of Verul

attractions.name: Bibi Ka Maqbara
attractions.description: The Mughal mausoleum inspired by the Taj Mahal, known as the Mini Taj of the Deccan.
about: Bibi Ka Maqbara is the iconic Mughal-era monument of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, built as the mausoleum of Rabia-ud-Durrani (Dilras Banu Begum), wife of the emperor Aurangzeb.

Its design was inspired by the Taj Mahal at Agra, which is why it is popularly known as the Mini Taj of the Deccan. The large central dome, four minarets, ornamental detailing and landscaped gardens make it one of the most recognisable landmarks of the region.
highlights: Design inspired by the Taj Mahal
whyVisit: One of the most photographed landmarks of the region
Well worth a half-day heritage visit

attractions.name: Ahilyabai Holkar Shivkund
attractions.description: A historic stepped water tank near Ellora with stone ghats and a calm spiritual atmosphere.
about: Ahilyabai Holkar Shivkund is a historic stepped water tank associated with the era of Ahilyabai Holkar, whose patronage also shaped the nearby Grishneshwar Temple.
The kund is known for its stone architecture, stepped ghats and small shrines around the water, and it offers a quiet pause between visits to the larger heritage sites of Verul and Ellora.
highlights: Stone architecture of the Ahilyabai Holkar era
Very close to Grishneshwar and Ellora
whyVisit: A calm heritage stop away from the crowds
Easy to combine with Grishneshwar Temple
